summary: This position paper frames intelligent delegation as a core systems problem for the agentic web, extending task assignment to include authority, accountability, monitoring, trust, and verification.
why_it_matters: It provides a rigorous conceptual layer for the task-allocation branch of the vault by connecting agent delegation to organizational theory, safety, and protocol design.
method_setup: The paper synthesizes ideas from multi-agent systems, hierarchical reinforcement learning, organizational theory, and cryptographic verification to propose a framework spanning task decomposition, assignment, monitoring, permissions, trust, and verifiable completion.
key_claims: Delegation in agent systems should include authority, accountability, and trust rather than task routing alone.
Future agent ecosystems need stronger protocols for monitoring, permissions, and liability.
Human organizational theory offers useful structure for designing safe delegation systems.
limitations: The work is conceptual and protocol-oriented rather than an implemented delegation platform.
Many of the most important claims still need real-world validation in large agent ecosystems.
